name: Portugal
snapshot: Socialist António José Seguro beat far-right André Ventura by about two to one in February 2026's presidential runoff, the first time the far right reached a final round.
culture: Fado, the mournful song of Lisbon and Coimbra, is UNESCO-listed and expresses saudade, a longing for something lost. Portugal's age of discovery left a language spoken by more than 250 million people. Pastel de nata, salt cod and port wine are national staples. Football, and Cristiano Ronaldo, are a passion.
society: Portugal has recovered from its debt crisis and attracted tourists, digital nomads and foreign buyers, driving up rents in Lisbon and Porto. Ventura's Chega party became the main opposition in 2025. The country decriminalised personal drug use in 2001, a much-studied policy. Emigration of young graduates remains high.

story: Portugal spent half a century, since its 1974 Carnation Revolution ended dictatorship, as a country where the far right barely existed. That changed with Chega ("Enough"), founded in 2019 by a former TV football pundit, André Ventura, which became the main opposition party in May 2025, the country's third election in three years. In 2026 Ventura reached for the presidency.

The first round on 18 January was disrupted by deadly storms and floods in central and southern Portugal, which forced voting to be suspended in some areas; Ventura demanded the whole election be postponed. He came second with 23.5 percent behind the Socialist António José Seguro, becoming the first far-right candidate ever to reach a Portuguese runoff (AFP via BSS). On 8 February, Seguro, a 63-year-old former Socialist leader who had been out of politics for a decade, won the runoff with about two-thirds of the vote, as most of the centre and centre-right rallied behind him (NPR via Michigan Public). Ventura still took more than 1.5 million votes, his party's best result, and declared that Chega "will soon govern this country." The presidency is mostly ceremonial, but Portuguese presidents can dissolve parliament, a power that has mattered a great deal in a country that keeps going back to the polls.
briefing.power: A semi-presidential republic. The prime minister leads the government with the support of the 230-seat Assembly of the Republic; the directly elected president has limited executive power but can veto laws and dissolve parliament.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Luís Montenegro (Democratic Alliance); President António José Seguro, since March 2026.
